system.name: Blowfish
system.one_liner: a system providing elastic virtual-machine memory over disaggregated memory infrastructure

components.name: VM #1
components.role: source virtual machine giving up a cold page

components.name: VM #2
components.role: destination virtual machine receiving the reallocated page

components.name: Page Out
components.role: step 0: selects a cold page and swaps out its infrequently-used data ('Swap Data Out')

components.name: GVA
components.role: guest virtual address mapped to the cold page being reclaimed

components.name: Unmap GPT
components.role: unmaps the guest page table entry to release the cold page

components.name: GPA (IOVA)
components.role: guest physical / IO virtual address freed in VM #1 once the GPT entry is unmapped

components.name: GPA (IOVA)
components.role: new guest physical / IO virtual address that VM #2 receives once the page is marked available

components.name: Scan & Mark Invalid
components.role: hypervisor step 1: scans and marks the freed guest page invalid

components.name: Unmap EPT & IOPT
components.role: hypervisor step 2: unmaps the extended page table and I/O page table to reclaim the free host page

components.name: Map EPT & IOPT
components.role: hypervisor step 3: remaps EPT and IOPT for the destination VM (reverse of step 2)

components.name: Mark Available
components.role: hypervisor step 4: marks the remapped page available to the destination VM (reverse of step 1)

components.name: HPA
components.role: the single host physical address/page being unmapped from VM #1 and remapped to VM #2

flows.what: guest page table entry released during page-out
frees the guest physical address in VM #1
freed page handed to the hypervisor
invalidated page proceeds to EPT/IOPT unmap
reclaims the free host physical page
same host physical page remapped for VM #2
remapped page proceeds to being marked available
page becomes VM #2's new guest physical address

content.key_idea: Reclaiming a cold guest page swaps out its data and unmaps GPT/EPT/IOPT to free the host physical page, which the hypervisor remaps and marks available as a new GPA in another VM.
content.reading_order: Top-down in VM #1 (Page Out, GVA, Unmap GPT) into four numbered Hypervisor steps around a shared HPA box, then back up into VM #2's new GPA (IOVA).

summary: This figure walks through reallocating a cold memory page from VM #1 to VM #2 via guest-level swapping. In VM #1, a Page Out step (0) swaps the cold page's infrequently-used data out and unmaps its GPT entry, freeing its GPA (IOVA). The hypervisor then scans and marks the page invalid (step 1) and unmaps the corresponding EPT and IOPT (step 2) to reclaim the underlying host physical page (HPA). To reallocate that same HPA to VM #2, the hypervisor performs the reverse steps: mapping a new EPT and IOPT (step 3) and marking the page available (step 4), at which point it appears as a new GPA (IOVA) inside VM #2. The figure is a compact, two-color (red/slate-blue) box diagram illustrating background guest-level swapping machinery that the paper's memory-overcommitment design builds on, rather than the paper's own novel mechanism.
summary_zh: 该图示范将冷页从 VM1 重分配给 VM2：VM1 换出冷页数据并解除 GPT 映射；管理程序依次标记无效、解除 EPT/IOPT 回收宿主物理页（HPA），再反向映射并标记可用，成为 VM2 新 GPA。
notes: The index marks this figure's role as 'background' (section 2, Background and Related Work): it illustrates a pre-existing guest-level swapping/cold-memory-reclaim mechanism that the paper's own system builds on, not a newly proposed component, so all components are marked novel:false. layout-proposal: mirrored U-pipeline — a numbered reclaim sequence descends from VM #1 into the Hypervisor/HPA, then a mirrored remap sequence ascends back up into VM #2 sharing the same HPA foundation; closest named template is pipeline, but the U-shaped, foundation-sharing arrangement is atypical for a straight pipeline.
